text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited (PTCL) has announced 12 per cent cash dividend for its share-holders for the year ending June 30, 1997, which comes to 0.60 rupees per share.
- Federal Shariat Court (FSC) admitted a review petition filed by the government seeking revision of the court's judgment on abolishing Riba.
- Opposition in Senate (upper house) accused the government of violating the constitution by illegally extraditing Aimal Kansi to the United States.
- Maulana Umar Hayyat, an active member of Sipah-e-Sihaba Pakistan, was gunned down by two motorcyclists in Lahore.
- Two construction workers were killed and more than 35 others trapped when a completed five-storey building, Faiza Heights, collapsed in North Karachi.
- The federal cabinet has abolished the existing Railway Board and decided to take up the issue of government's downsizing in a special meeting to be convened next week.

- A U.S. circuit court has set November 3 as the date for the trial of CIA fugitive Mir Aimal Kansi, after disallowing live telecasts of the trial and refusing to put a general gag order on comment about the case.
- The Central Board of Revenue has detected a tax fraud which might turn out to be one of the biggest in the history of tax collection in Pakistan, involving more than 500 industrial units.

- American Management Association, a U.S.-based company, has suggested after a survey of Pakistan's corporate sector that the government set up a quality foundation to encourage and recognise companies which excel in quality.
- The Pakistan National Shipping Corporation earned an estimated profit of 59 million rupees in fiscal 1995/96 (July-June).
- The federal cabinet has approved a wheat flour subsidy scheme for under-privileged people.
- The federal cabinet is being expanded by another seven to eight members in the next two days, a competent source said.
- Water and Power Minister Nisar Ali Khan said the new power policy would emphasise development of hydro-electric power.
